svg.aria-label: QTrade's real architecture, 2026-08-27, third pass: order latency lives entirely inside SimExchange, split into a real outbound leg and a real inbound leg, with the Scheduler used to guarantee resolution even in a quiet market. Two flows are shown. Setup-time, once, before replay begins: the strategy's on_start calls ctx.subscribe, which goes from Strategy to ControlDispatcher, which registers the route with EventDispatcher -- dashed arrows, since this never repeats. Runtime, once per real event: main.rs schedules two MarketData events per capture record, one at exchange_ts targeting SimExchange and one at recorder_ts targeting Cache; when a real market event fires, main.rs calls SimExchange directly, then ExecutionEngine turns the resulting reports into an ExecOutcome which flows back through main.rs and immediately onward to ControlDispatcher, which calls the strategy's on_fill or on_order_update -- one connected path, not two independent calls. Separately, when a subscribed book changes, EventDispatcher wakes the strategy through Ctx, whose ctx.submit, cancel, or modify calls ExecutionEngine's gate check and its venue delivery back to back, synchronously, in the same instant, with no Scheduler reference in that path at all. SimExchange itself holds a submitted order in an internal queue and matches it only once its own real outbound delay has elapsed, holding the resulting report a further real inbound delay before it becomes visible -- and because a real exchange answers at its own processing time regardless of what else happens, main.rs also keeps one OrderArrival alarm and one ReportDelivery alarm in sync with whatever SimExchange itself says it is waiting on, so a quiet market can never leave an order unresolved past its true due time.
svg.text: QTrade — Architecture (order latency lives in the venue)

Solid arrows: the per-event runtime loop. Dashed arrows: one-time setup, during on_start. Order/cancel/modify calls reach SimExchange immediately — the outbound/inbound delay, and the alarm that guarantees it resolves, are the venue's own business.

main.rs — constructs every engine below, owns the one real Scheduler (now used only for the two MarketData events per record), and is the only place that pattern-matches a popped event (dispatch_event)

Real, 21_08_2026: every Submitted→Filled gap is now exactly 500,000ns (250,000 outbound + 250,000 inbound) — the alarm resolves each order at its true due time, not whenever the next real tick happens to arrive.
